Rashi on Niddah 23a:10:1.english: Since their eyes - [Those] of a wild animal and a domesticated animal.

Rashi on Niddah 23a:10:2.hebrew: דומות לשל אדם - שחור שבעין הוה עגול בבהמה כשל אדם, אבל דדגים לאו עגול הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:10:2.english: Similar to those of a human - The black [part] of the eye is round in [a land] animal, like that of a human, but that of fish is not round.

Rashi on Niddah 23a:13:1.hebrew: והא גבי מומין תני לה - כלומר, היכי אמרת דעין בהמה דומה לאדם? והא גבי מומי הבכור קתני לה בבכורות (דף מ.) ושגלגל עינו הוי מום. ומדחשיב ליה מום, נמצא שאין דרך בהמה להיות עיניה כאדם:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:13:1.english: But with regard to blemishes, it is taught - That is to say: How can you say that the eye of an animal is similar to that of a human? But with regard to the blemishes of a firstborn animal, it is taught in [tractate] Bekhorot (40a) that [an animal] whose pupil [is round like a human's] is [considered] blemished. And since [the mishna] considers it a blemish, it turns out that it is not the way of animals for their eyes to be like those of a human.

Rashi on Niddah 23a:13:2.hebrew: באוכמא - שחור שבעין הוי עגול בבהמה כאדם. והא דתני דהוי מום, בציריא — מקום מושב כל העין — לא הוי עגול בבהמה כאדם, ואי הוי עגול הוי מום, דכל בור של מושב העין קרוי גלגל, כדאמרי' לקמן (נדה דף כד:) "ועמדתי בגלגל עינו של מת עד חוטמי", ומפני שהוא עגול כגלגל:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:13:2.english: With the pupil - The black [part] of the eye is round in an animal, like [that of] a human. And as for what is taught that it is a blemish, [this refers] to the socket — the place where the whole eye sits — which is not round in an animal like [it is] in a human; and if it were round, it would be a blemish. For the entire cavity in which the eye sits is called a "galgal," as we say below (Niddah 24b): "And I stood in the galgal of the eye of a corpse, up to my nose," because it is round like a wheel [galgal]:

Rashi on Niddah 23a:14:1.hebrew: לפניהם - לאפוקי דגים, דעיניהם בצדיהם, וכן נחש:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:14:1.english: In front of them - This excludes fish, whose eyes are on their sides, and likewise a snake.

Rashi on Niddah 23a:16:1.hebrew: קריא וקיפופא - עוף הצועק בלילה, ופניו דומה לחתול, ועיניו לפניו:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:16:1.english: The little owl and the great owl - A bird that cries out at night, whose face resembles a cat's, and whose eyes are in front [of its head].

Rashi on Niddah 23a:18:1.hebrew: חסורי מיחסרא והכי קתני נראין דברי ר"מ בבהמה ובחיה והוא הדין לקריא וקיפופא - דעיניו הולכו' לפניו, ואע"פ דפליגי רבנן עליה:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:18:1.english: It is lacking, and this is what it teaches: The words of Rabbi Meir seem [correct] regarding a domesticated animal and an undomesticated animal, and the same applies to a little owl and a great owl - For its eyes are directed forward, even though the Rabbis disagree with him.

Rashi on Niddah 23a:18:2.hebrew: ודברי חכמים - נראין אפילו לר"מ בשאר עופות, דר"מ נמי מודה להו:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:18:2.english: And the statement of the Rabbis - appears correct even to Rabbi Meir with regard to other birds, for Rabbi Meir also concedes to them.

Rashi on Niddah 23a:19:1.english: And it was taught - [This is stated] calmly [i.e., not as a challenge].

Rashi on Niddah 23a:1:1.hebrew: להכי אפנייה רחמנא כו' - דהאי מופנה משני צדדין כרבנן:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:1:1.english: For this reason the Merciful One rendered it free, etc. - [This is] according to the Rabbis.

Rashi on Niddah 23a:1:2.hebrew: דלא תגמר ממופנה מצד אחד - משום דמשיבין, וכאן יש להשיב: מה לאיש שכן מטמא מחיים, כדלקמיה:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:1:2.english: So that it not be derived from [an analogy] free on one side - Because one can refute it, and here there is room to refute: What [is true] of a man, since he imparts impurity while alive, as [stated] below.

Rashi on Niddah 23a:22:1.hebrew: ומאי שנא קריא וקיפופא - דקאמר לרבנן דהוי ולד טפי משאר עופות, אי משום דעיניהם הולכות לפניהם — הרי חיה ובהמה נמי דעיניהן הולכות לפניהם, ופליגי רבנן:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:22:1.english: And what is different [about] a little owl and a great owl - [Why] does he say, according to the Rabbis, that [the discharge] is [considered] a child more than [in the case of] other birds? If [it is] because their eyes face forward — behold, a wild animal and a domesticated animal also have eyes that face forward, and yet the Rabbis disagree [and rule that these are not a child]:

Rashi on Niddah 23a:22:2.hebrew: לסתות - לחיים זקופין כאדם, מה שאין כן בבהמה ובחיה:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:22:2.english: Cheeks - Upright jaws like [those of] a human, which is not so in a domesticated animal or an undomesticated animal.

Rashi on Niddah 23a:24:1.hebrew: למימרא דחיי - הא אחותה לא מיתסרא אלא בחייה, דאין איסור אחות אשה אלא בחייה:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:24:1.english: Is this to say that it lives? - For her sister is prohibited only during her [the wife's] lifetime, as the prohibition of a wife's sister applies only during her [the wife's] lifetime.

Rashi on Niddah 23a:2:1.hebrew: לקולא - דלא בעינן מופנה כולי האי:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:2:1.english: To be lenient - For we do not require [a verbal analogy to be] free to such an extent:

Rashi on Niddah 23a:2:2.hebrew: לרבנן - כיון דלמופנה מצד אחד למדין ומשיבין, ולשאינו מופנה כל עיקר אמרינן דברי הכל למדין ומשיבין, מאי איכא בין מופנה מצד אחד לשאינה מופנה כל עיקר?:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:2:2.english: According to the Rabbis - Since for [a verbal analogy] free on one side, [the Rabbis hold that] one derives and one refutes, and for one that is not free at all, we say that everyone agrees that one derives and one refutes, what is the difference between [an analogy] free on one side and one that is not free at all?

Rashi on Niddah 23a:5:1.hebrew: והכא מאי פירכא איכא - כלומר, והכא בג"ש דתני אאדם, מה תשובה איכא? דקאמרת דניחא לך למיגמר מחיה דהוי מופנה משני צדדין, משום דאין משיבין, ולא נגמר בריאה בריאה מתנין, משום דמופנה מצד אחד הוא ומשיבין, ומאי אית לך לאותובי:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:5:1.english: And here, what refutation is there? - That is to say: And here, with regard to the verbal analogy [gezera shava] of the one taught concerning man, what answer is there? For you say that it is preferable to you to derive from chayya ["living creature"], which is free on both sides, because one cannot refute it, and not to derive [by the analogy of] "creature, creature" from the sea monster, because it is free on only one side and one can refute it. And what [refutation] do you have to raise?

Rashi on Niddah 23a:5:2.hebrew: שכן מטמא מחיים - מקבל טומאה בחייו משרץ או משאר טומאות. דין הוא שתהא יולדתו טמאה לידה — תאמר באלו! הלכך גבי דגים פרכינן ליה, דמופנה מצד אחד הוא. אבל גבי בהמה, אע"ג דפירכא היא, לא פרכינן לה, הואיל ומופנה היא משני צדדין:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:5:2.english: Since it becomes impure while alive - It receives impurity during its lifetime from a creeping creature or from other sources of impurity. [The refutation continues:] It is logical that one who gives birth to it should be impure with the impurity of childbirth — [to which one can respond:] You may say this regarding these [cases, i.e., humans]! Therefore, with regard to fish we refute it, since it is free on one side only. But with regard to an animal, even though there is a refutation, we do not refute it, since it is free on both sides.

Rashi on Niddah 23a:6:1.hebrew: וכן אמר רבי חייא כו' - אדרב יהודה אמר שמואל קאי:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:6:1.english: And likewise Rabbi Chiyya said, etc. - It refers back to [the statement of] Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel.

Rashi on Niddah 23a:7:1.hebrew: הר מי קמפלת - וכי מי מפלת נפל גדול כהר?
Rashi on Niddah 23a:7:1.english: Does she discharge a mountain? - Does a woman discharge a fetus as large as a mountain?

Rashi on Niddah 23a:7:2.hebrew: דמות אבן הוא דמפלת - חתיכת בשר דמות אבן. גוש בעלמא מיקרי, ולא כתיבא ביה יצירה:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:7:2.english: It is the form of a stone that she discharges - A piece of flesh in the form of a stone. It is called merely a clod, and "forming" is not written regarding it.

Rashi on Niddah 23a:7:3.hebrew: גוש - כמו (איוב ז) גוש עפר:
Rashi on Niddah 23a:7:3.english: Clod - Like [the verse] (Job 7) “a clod of dust.”

Tosafot on Niddah 23a:11:1.hebrew: ליתני נחש - ואע"ג דקתני חיה, ונחש בכלל חיה, כדכתיב (בראשית ג׳:א׳): "והנחש היה ערום מכל חית השדה" — לאחר שנקצצו רגליו לא מיקרי חיה סתם, אלא חיה הרומשת, ולא הוי בכלל חיה דמתניתין:
Tosafot on Niddah 23a:11:1.english: Let it teach "a snake" - But even though [the mishna] teaches "a beast," and a snake is included in [the category of] "beast," as it is written (Genesis 3:1): "Now the serpent was more cunning than any beast of the field" — [nevertheless,] after its legs were cut off it is no longer called simply a "beast," but rather a creeping beast, and it is not included in the "beast" of the mishna:

Tosafot on Niddah 23a:18:1.hebrew: קריא וקיפופא - ג' מיני קיפוף יש: הכוס והינשוף (ויקרא יא) מתרגמינן "קריא וקיפופא", והתנשמת נמי. אמר באלו טריפות (חולין דף סג.): זה באות שבעופות, ואמר אביי: באות שבעופות קיפוף. ועוד, קיפוף מין חיה, כדאמר בהרואה (ברכות נז:): כל מיני חיה יפין לחלום, חוץ מן הקוף והקיפוף:
Tosafot on Niddah 23a:18:1.english: Kariya and kipupa - There are three kinds of kipuf [owl]: the kos and the yanshuf (Leviticus 11), which we translate [in the Targum] as "kariya and kipupa," and also the tinshemet. [The Gemara] states in [the chapter] Eilu Terefot (Chullin 63a): This is the one that comes among the birds; and Abaye said: The one that comes among the birds is the kipuf. Furthermore, kipuf is a kind of undomesticated animal, as stated in [the chapter] Ha-Roeh (Berakhot 57b): All kinds of undomesticated animals are good [to see] in a dream, except for the monkey and the kipuf.

Tosafot on Niddah 23a:1:1.hebrew: וילפינן ממופנה משני צדדין - תימה: ולשתוק מהפנאה דאדם, דהשתא תנין לא מופנה כלל, ובהמה מופנה בצד אחד, ואין משיבין:
Tosafot on Niddah 23a:1:1.english: And we derive from [an analogy] that is free on both sides - It is puzzling: Let [the verse] be silent about the freeing on the part of man, for now [the analogy of] the sea monster is not free at all, and [that of] the animal is free on one side, and one does not refute [such an analogy].

Tosafot on Niddah 23a:23:1.hebrew: לאיתסורי באחותה - לענין גופה לא בעי: אם הבא עליה חייב משום אשת איש, או אם חייב ההורגה, דפשיטא ליה דאינה חיה ג' שנים שתהא בת ביאה, ולא שנה שלא תהא טרפה. ומיהו הוה מצי למבעי אם הרובע חייב סקילה כדין הבא על הבהמה:
Tosafot on Niddah 23a:23:1.english: To be prohibited [to marry] her sister - With regard to the animal itself, he did not ask [whether] one who has relations with her is liable for [relations with] a married woman, or whether one who kills her is liable [for murder], for it is obvious to him that she does not live three years so as to be fit for intercourse, nor [even] a year so as not to be a tereifah. However, he could have asked whether one who mates with her [i.e., one who has relations with the animal] is liable to stoning, like the law of one who has relations with an animal:

Tosafot on Niddah 23a:7:1.hebrew: יוצר הרים - ומופנה הוא, כדקאמר בסמוך:
Tosafot on Niddah 23a:7:1.english: “He Who forms the mountains” - And it is superfluous [i.e., the verse is not needed for its plain meaning], as [the Gemara] says shortly afterward:
